messages:
sara: Hey team — several customers hit parser failures when using structured JSON mode on /v1/generate. They get "invalid JSON" or client exceptions when an array of nested objects is returned. Posting minimal repro and raw response. @devon @matt

devon: Can you paste the exact raw response and SDK/lang/version?

sara: Repro curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"xlarge-2","structured":true,"prompt":"summarize input"}'
```
And the raw body the client received (they hit a parse error):
```
{
  "id": "resp_def",
  "choices": [
    {"index":0,"delta":{"text":"{\"items\":[{\"id\":"a1\",\"score\":0.92},{\"score\":0.73}]}"}},
    {"index":1,"delta":{"text":"\n"}}
  ],
  "meta": {"duration_ms":134}
}
```
Note: the second element in items is missing the required "id" key. Several downstream parsers assume that field exists and fail. Some customers also complained that item ordering changed between calls which their code depended on.

matt: Two likely contributors: (1) streaming/delta assembly can produce partial fragments if client concatenation is naive, and (2) routing to a fallback model variant that uses a different schema where id is optional. @jess any insight from structured-mode validation?

jess: Streaming can indeed emit fragments, but an entirely missing required key points to a schema variant or truncation. Check routing and fallback. Also worth noting: our structured output contract doesn't promise stable array ordering unless explicitly annotated.

support-rotate: Customer said this began after weekend deploy. They also saw intermittent 401s earlier in the morning. Could billing-induced routing be involved? @billing-bot any holds around that time for the org?

billing-bot: Alert: org_789 entered a soft billing hold at 2024-11-10T03:00:00Z. Fallback applied via fallback_policy=compatible_model -> small-compat. See billing ticket #3500.

devon: I pulled routing logs for request resp_def: the request was routed to small-compat at 2024-11-10T03:00:02Z. That model's advertised structured spec marks items[].id as optional. That would explain the missing key.

matt: Opening INF-802 to address this. Proposed fixes: (a) add strict schema validation in the response pipeline when structured=true and return 409 with structured_schema_mismatch if output doesn't fit declared schema, (b) temporarily post-process to insert nulls for required fields and emit schema_mismatch telemetry, (c) enhance routing guards so fallback models must advertise compatible structured specs or requests fail fast.

sara: Repro steps for eng to validate: (1) create a test org, (2) apply a soft billing hold, (3) call /v1/generate with structured=true and a prompt producing items array, (4) compare shape between primary and fallback. Example quick check: 
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"xlarge-2","structured":true,"prompt":"list items"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | jq .
```
Then flip the soft-hold and re-run.

jess: Docs/UX mitigation: update structured-output.md to clarify arrays are unordered unless annotated, and call out that fallback models may return slimmer schemas. Also add guidance for clients to use tolerant parsing by filling defaults.

support-rotate: Customer-facing note drafted: "We identified that a billing soft-hold caused traffic to route to a fallback model variant with a slightly different structured JSON schema. This can remove fields or change array order, causing parsers to fail. Workarounds: (1) restore billing to return to primary model, (2) set accept_schema_mismatch=false to force the request to fail with a clear error, or (3) use tolerant parsing that supplies defaults for missing keys. We're shipping server-side schema validation (INF-802)."

api-bot: New support ticket #3500 created and linked to INF-802. Priority: P1. Assigned: matt, jess.

sara: Marking this P1. If we can't ship a guard in 48h, add to release blocker. Thanks everyone.

devon: I'll include a retro note for postmortem. :thumbsup:

support-rotate: Closing thread after customer notified; keeping INF-802 open for engineering follow-up.
